During the course of the study of the transmission line network, we investigated the condition of insulators and conductor cables, and the degree of steel structures corrosion in the ground area of the utility towers. The report proposes that despite the intended installation of a combination of optical fiber cable and earth wire it is possible to refurbish the transmission links without undertaking major structural changes on the steel towers. The report describes the problems that must be solved in undertaking such measures.

articleTitle: Supply quality in planning of MV networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Improving the daily quality of delivery and gaining control over large scale failures that occur on the network, while mastering investment costs, are two key sectors of the quality policy of EDF for the period 1995-2005. As medium voltage networks play an extremely important role in electricity supply, it appeared essential to develop a planning tool enabling the operator to make strategic choice on investments, that takes into account the above-mentioned quality policy. Of course, this decision making aid should be able to perform electrical calculations as well. Designed for Windows, PRAO 2.0 software can fulfil this need. Today it constitutes both the reference software tool in EDF for MV network studies and the cornerstone for its international proposal.

articleTitle: Digital protection and monitoring system for medium voltage substations and electric installations
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: A new approach to substation control and protection, aimed at the improvement of the management of power networks and substations, is being advocated by manufacturers and adopted by increasing numbers of power supply authorities. Protection, substation local control, operator interfaces, communication, remote control and a host of monitoring functions, most of which were previously segregated and device-oriented, with discrete relays or modules for each function, are now being integrated into multi-function microprocessor based units and interconnected on various types of local area networks. So, every component communicates to each other, sharing information through the local area network, and systems are smaller, because only one sensor is necessary for each information, instead of one sensor per component as before. The report defines the notion of a "target architecture" that manufacturers should focus on as far as interoperability is concerned in protection and monitoring control systems for electric substations. It presents a model of an integrated digital system that might provide the answer. This model is currently available and is well adapted to medium voltage electrical installations in industrial networks.

articleTitle: Testing a 110 kV external gas pressure cable to evaluate continued operational reliability
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: After several disruptive discharges during operation of an external gas pressure cable manufactured in 1953, it was decided to investigate the causes of these failures in the laboratory. At the same time, the opportunity was taken to apply various methods of diagnosis that have been developed for evaluating ageing, plastic insulated cables so as to test whether the use of such measurement methods suited to on-site applications can also supply meaningful results for this type of layered dielectric. The authors discuss the cable design, describe the failure, and discuss the test methods to check the diagnostic procedures.

articleTitle: Dielectric measurements for diagnosis of XPLE cable insulation
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: A research project was started in 1992 with the aim to develop a useful nondestructive method to determine the condition of water tree deteriorated XLPE cables in service. Since 1995 an extensive laboratory investigation has been made on cables aged in service and a large number of field measurements have been performed on cables in service. The purpose of this report is to present these results and the further development of the diagnostic procedures. This report starts with presentation of the measurement procedure. The procedure is applied both to laboratory and field measurements. In the part on laboratory investigations the ability to detect deteriorated cables is verified and measured dielectric response is related to breakdown voltages. The application of the method on cables in service is then presented. The field investigation part also includes practical considerations on the measurement procedure and on the influence of accessories and terminations.

articleTitle: Improvement of substation maintenance
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: This paper presents the way of idea and practice of Dalian Electric Power Supply Company (DPSC) concerning transformation of substation equipment maintenance strategy from the time-based periodical maintenance to state-based state maintenance (also called foresighted maintenance). The key to this state maintenance lies in the profound grasp of the principle information of equipment state and enhancement of whole-time course management (longitudinal) over each individual equipment and comprehensive (transversal) management over all the equipment. This paper also introduces some monitoring devices developed by DPSC for this purpose and the information management system of equipment state, which is now under construction.

articleTitle: A philosophy and algorithms for extinguishing earth fault arcs in suppressed medium voltage networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The compensation of earth fault current in medium voltage power networks can be carried out either centrally or by using more cost-effective decentralized compensation. This paper introduces a novel cost-effective principle for increasing the compensation degree and selecting the tripping range of earth fault relays in originally partially compensated or isolated power systems. This has an essentially positive effect on the reduction of short interruptions to customers. Earth faults in compensated systems are simulated by the ATP version of the well-known EMTP program and the results are compared to field measurements. Conditions in radially operated rural 20 kV overhead line networks are considered.

articleTitle: On-site examination for predicting the remaining life-time of paper and synthetic insulated cables
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: On-site, nondestructive examination of long and medium voltage paper-, polyethylene-, and PVC insulated cables is rather difficult with 50 Hz frequency at nominal voltage due to the excess power consumption and network disturbances. But the benefit of these tests is that the parameters and limits which result have been fairly accurately and reliably determined after long experience acquired through laboratory tests of short cable sections. For solving this problem, DEDASZ Rt. has been studying its old paper-, polyethylene-, and PVC insulated cables for 5 years, after a cable diagnostic vehicle was developed. Analysis, especially as follow-up after a cable failure, is important in planning for cable replacement. This paper describes the special testing device and the on-site methods for measuring capacitance, loss factor, partial discharge, and the changing of parameters as a function of voltage. Once the rate of deterioration over time is known, with the help of a computer the remaining life of the cables can be determined with reasonable accuracy, based on the results of regular measurements. The life extension of two long cables by replacing the old cables in sections is described in this paper. Finally, background on the diagnosis of 4 complete cable replacements is presented.

articleTitle: Monitoring of states and preventive maintenance [of distribution networks]
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: GEC Alsthom T&D is satisfying the increasing demand for monitoring of states by the use of modern sensors made intelligent and capable of communication by means of electronic progress. These sensors are used for a wide variety of purposes including temperature measurements and the measurement of magnitudes such as the rate of movement of breaking devices useful for preventive maintenance, and are placed at judicious locations within medium voltage distribution cubicles. Information output from these sensors may be transmitted directly in "on-off" form, or in coded form through a standard field bus. Communicating remote inputs-outputs are used for this purpose. Remote inputs-outputs can be configured by software, by an operator without computer experience. This software is installed onsite, and displays the state of breaking devices and can also remotely control them. The preventive maintenance plan is adapted as a function of information originating from these sensors. This adaptation can be done by specialists in the factory who make use of the remote contents of a database updated by information originating from these sensors.

articleTitle: Source based protection of wind farms using a multi-function protection relay-its design and site trial experience
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Laboratory simulation, relay testing and a site trial have been used to both validate and develop a new type of protection for small to medium sized wind farms (0-20 MW). The protection, implemented within a multifunction relay, is sufficiently sensitive to detect all realistic in-zone faults and correctly discriminates with the LV fuses that detect LV cable faults. Similarly, the site trial has confirmed that the source based protection is stable during out-of-zone faults and other types of network disturbances.

articleTitle: Connectors for aluminium cable: a review of the different technologies and their interaction with cable accessories
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Problems encountered in medium voltage power cable connections have gained importance recently, as a consequence of numerous phenomena. Internationally, there are more and more accounts of mounting problems and problems with the right choice of connector. Here, the authors try to clarify the actual situation by means of theoretical considerations and test results.

articleTitle: Distribution transformer for the 21st Century
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: An advanced distribution transformer design as well as the superior properties of a new synthetic fluid resulted in a power transformer that is significantly smaller and of lighter weight. In addition, the transformer provides many environmental benefits including the use of significantly less fluid, and the excellent environmental properties of the synthetic fluid. The new transformer is more "trouble-free" throughout its life. The transformer is easier to handle and install; it is dependable and able to handle extreme conditions. Also, the use of recycling programs and the new environmentally preferable fluid reduce both product disposal and fluid spill clean-up concerns.

articleTitle: Dynamic resource planning applied to distribution transformers
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The large number of currently installed distribution transformers in Iberdrola-nearly 90,000 units-and the wide range of output rates, primary voltages, secondary voltages, types of dielectric, class of cover-passes, etc. into which these transformers can be subdivided, has to date made it very difficult to optimise the number of standby transformers and procurement of new units. This situation is further complicated by the large land area covered by the distribution grid /spl sim/28 provinces in Spain and nearly 50 stores. This paper describes how, with this background, a system to aid decision making in the assignment of transformers (SADMAT) has been drawn up which will help in the procurement of transformers from outside sources.

articleTitle: A review of the incidence of medium and high voltage overhead electric power lines in causing forest fires
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Overhead high voltage lines design has traditionally been subject of controversy because their possible environmental impact. Nevertheless, the benefits derived from the use of electric energy and the need to transport it have finally forced the actual situation. Among the possible risks attached to overhead lines (both high and low voltage), these elements have been often blamed for causing forest fires. The project presented in this paper (IMPACFALTAS) is oriented to investigate the possible relation between forest fires and overhead high voltage lines. In the research completed so far, the effect of medium voltage (MV) lines (up to 33 kV) on the Mediterranean forest species have been studied in detail, being the main objective of the study to help in the diagnosis, prevent their consequences and mitigate the effects of the accidents that are somehow likely to produce this kind of fire.

articleTitle: Metering and energy management in the environment of a de-regulated electricity market
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: In Finland, a de-regulated electricity market was opened on the first of November 1995. For electric power companies this caused big changes. Customers now have the right to choose their power suppliers. The power network operation and energy sales which have formerly been jointly organised by one company, are now separate businesses and the power network operator has to transmit the electric power on equal terms regardless from whom the customers purchase their power. In this paper, the problems of energy management from the standpoint of the energy selling and distributing companies in the new situation are discussed. The topics covered are: the estimation of hourly energy demands; optimisation of energy purchases; short-term trade management; and retail tariff design.

articleTitle: Lightning protection means for XLPE-covered conductors as integral parts of the line insulation
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Overhead power lines with XLPE-covered conductors must be protected against flashover due to lightning. Applying spark gaps in all phases causes a short-circuit between phases which may not comply with the power quality requirements. Substituting the gaps by arresters is a questionable solution due to the expected energy stresses on the arresters. This paper presents a combined solution applicable to networks with nonsolid grounded neutrals. The top conductor is protected by spark gaps and acts as a shielding wire for the two other phase conductors. Arresters are used to prevent backflashover. The energy stresses on these arresters are very moderate except when shielding failure occurs. It is, however, possible to obtain an acceptable arrester failure rate by keeping the risk of shielding failure sufficiently low. Several practical designs of the pole top are discussed and the potentially most attractive ones use arresters whose casing has sufficient mechanical strength to eliminate the need for the conventional line-insulators.

articleTitle: Time domain solution of arcing faults detection and fault distance calculation on distribution lines
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: A new numerical algorithm for blocking automatic reclosing on power distribution lines with permanent symmetrical or unsymmetrical faults is presented. It can be utilized in the field of distance protection and fault location. Through numerous computer simulations it is concluded that the algorithm is not sensitive on the higher order harmonics and decaying DC component presented in the input signals (line terminal voltages and currents). A very interesting example of laboratory testing is also presented, confirming the excellent results obtained in computer simulations.

articleTitle: Overvoltage protection for MV-substations
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: In the past, MV substations, which were fed via cable link with the overhead line, were often destroyed due to lightning flashes. These damages occurred although the unit substations are in general protected by a surge arrester at the cable/overhead line conjunction against lightning overvoltages. This protection is in many cases insufficient to avoid an overstress of the substation. For this reason, the installation of an additional surge arrester inside the substation is necessary. In this paper, a protection scheme against overvoltages concerning these MV substations is developed and recommended which takes into account that an overstress due to a lightning flash should be avoided. Due to the increased service of SF/sub 6/-insulated metal-enclosed switchgear in the medium voltage range, the overvoltage protection of such equipment will be more important in the future.

articleTitle: Behaviour of XLPE insulated medium voltage cables in long duration immersion
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: For a certain number of years the behaviour of medium voltage power cables with synthetic insulation in a wet environment has been discussed. More recently, some countries have tried to develop several long-duration test methods to better understand power cable behaviour under such conditions. 20 years ago, France developed a power cable model with radial and lengthwise watertightness. Despite this specificity and in order to have an input to the tests carried out in Europe, this type of power cable has been under further investigation to understand its behaviour when the insulation is in the presence of water. Tests consisted mainly of ageing the cable in water at 50/spl deg/C under four times its rated voltage for two years. Residual voltage strength has been measured after six months, one year and two years. As observed in other laboratories, a drop of voltage strength mainly occurs during the first six months. This report gives detailed results from these experiments, thus updating the results presented at JICABLE 95.

articleTitle: Advanced decentralised control system for MV/LV distribution system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Decentralised control systems for the automation of MV and LV electrical distribution networks are today possible thanks to the availability of more and more powerful intelligent devices. These devices are integrated in circuit-breakers and switchboards. Intelligent devices are directly connected via field-buses and can communicate with each other. The paper describes how to carry out the automation required by the distribution network using intelligent devices. This goal can be achieved without the use of a centralised controller. As a consequence, it is possible to save resources, improve quality, reduce design and engineering time and increase power system flexibility.

articleTitle: Recycling of cable waste
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The project "Recycling of cable waste" has been executed by KEMA Nederland in order to determine how much cable waste is recycled today and can be recycled in the future. By making an inventory of modern recycling processes for several types of cables and testing these processes on an industrial scale, the potential of cable recycling is demonstrated. Besides a further recovery of metals, the feasibility of plastics recycling from particular waste streams has been shown in this project. After recovering 90% of the metals from distribution cables, a plastic waste stream containing 80% PVC, 10% (XL)PE, 5% rubber and 5% metal was obtained. Firstly, the metal content was further decreased to 0.3% by using an electrostatic separator, recovering 85% of the residual metal. Secondly, in order to recycle the PVC had to be separated. The PVC can not be separated with conventional technologies due to a density overlap of the PVC and the rubber. By using a tribo-electric separator PVC with a purity of more than 98% was produced. This product can be purified by melt filtration to obtain a reusable PVC.

articleTitle: Aspects concerning power distribution networks planning using artificial intelligence
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: This paper presents the application of AI tools for the on-line identification of load structure in distribution networks. The authors have considered artificial neural networks (ANN) which are known as valuable and fast tools for pattern identification or completion. This approach to the load model allows a more detailed analysis directed towards the optimization of system structure and working conditions. Traditional methods produce good results but raise the processing time problem, especially when applied to large systems. For such cases another approach uses genetic algorithms, which are frequently referenced in the literature concerned with power distribution systems (reconfiguration of open loop radial networks, optimal VAr-sources distribution, optimal selection of transformer tap position).

articleTitle: Distribution power quality improvements using DC links with battery storage in existing networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The use of DC links with battery storage in LV distribution networks provides several advantages for both the final user and the electric utility. In particular, with the use of DC links between the LV windings of the distribution transformers and the load, the following advantages can be obtained: improvement of the power quality of the energy supplied to the user, in particular because the DC link with battery storage can eliminate short voltage interruptions and dips of up to a few minutes; and possibility of using a higher voltage level for the DC line than those presently used for AC lines, thus increasing the link power carrying capability. These features are very important in urban areas, where the installation of new power cables is costly (and sometimes very difficult to realise) and the request for power quality is ever increasing due to the growth in the number of electronic appliances. In this paper, several possible alternatives for realising such a DC link are presented and their feasibility is shown, both in terms of normal and faulty operation and of reliability. Some economic considerations are also dealt with, with particular attention given to a case study.

articleTitle: Experience with SINAI an integrated incident analysis system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: SINAI is a computer system for collecting, analysing, storing and accessing all the information generated by SCADA, digital protection and recording equipment about the incidents that happen in the electrical network. This paper presents the experiences that have been noted by IBERDROLA from last June to date, during the testing period. Of course, the authors hope that these results are worse than those which will be obtained in 1997 when the system will be completely finished and working. The results are analysed and compared with those obtained in the past with conventional tools. Because of a delay in the development of the project, this report has been written before the system will be in operation, which will happen next January. In the CIRED 97 conference that will be held in June, real operating data of the system will be provided.

articleTitle: Study on features of ferromagnetic resonance 110 kV substation and it's eliminating method
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Based on the oscillograms recorded during tests of ferromagnetic resonance in many 110 kV substations, this paper reveals some important features which are not yet known and different from that in a 10-66 kV neutral isolated system. It also suggests a method, by the aid of zero sequence channel of the open delta winding of potential transformer, as well as the assistance of introducing a positive sequence auxiliary line into the resonance circuit as a damper, to eliminate the resonance both of zero sequence and positive sequence nature. Based on this method a computer-aided resonance eliminating device, using thyristors as damping elements, has been developed and operated successfully in some substations in China for five years. This paper also introduces the structural principle of this device.

articleTitle: Diagnostic maintenance management system for MV and HV substations
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: At many electric utilities, maintenance processes are changing by two major influences, which relate to market conditions and technical limitations, respectively. This paper describes how, on order to meet both of these challenges, KEMA has developed (in co-operation with the other Dutch utilities) a new diagnostic expert support system-based maintenance management methodology, called MainMan(R).

articleTitle: The behaviour of medium voltage cable terminations at artificial pollution
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Terminations for medium voltage cables are mainly produced from plastic insulating materials. Under outdoor conditions electrolytic conductive layers are developed on the surface of the insulation caused by pollution and moisture. The applied operating voltage leads to a leakage current often being combined with partial discharges on the surface. The energy of these discharges results in an erosion of the surface. Following pollutants, as well as moisture, adhere to the surface. In the case of incorrect selection of the insulating material (nontracking resistant) or of unfavourable design of the termination, conductive tracking traces can occur, leading rapidly to the failure of the termination. The insulation behaviour under such conditions is proven by means of the so called salt-fog-test. The demonstration of test results of various termination designs gives a contribution to an improved interpretation, as well as an evaluation of the technical reserves.

articleTitle: Speed control of DC motor drives based on efficient utilization of energy and optimal performance
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The most flexible control is obtained by means of a separately-excited DC motor, in which the armature and field circuits are provided with separate sources. The speed control in a DC motor is widely applied. The concept of control system optimization comprises a selection of a performance criterion and a design which yields the optimal control system subjective to the limits imposed by physical constraint, which will minimize some measure of deviation from ideal behaviour. In addition to considering errors as a measure of system performance, however, it must pay attention to the energy required for the control action, for efficient utilization of energy, since the control input is proportional to the required energy. If the errors are minimized regardless of the energy required, then a design may result in an overly large value of control input. The discrete optimal control theory in addition to the preview feedforward control, which depends on minimizing a selected performance index, are involved in the design of a system controller to obtain the optimal control law. Simulation results are obtained to investigate the effectiveness, the susceptibility, the feasibility and the transient response properties of the above mentioned system. An experimental set-up is built up to confirm the above obtained simulation results. A three phase six-pulse power converter is built to provide a variable DC power supply to the armature circuit, controlled either manually or automatically through an analog DC voltage applied from a microcomputer, in order to decrease power loss and improve the utilization of energy.

articleTitle: Load flow calculations on distribution networks by using a statistical approach
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The availability of automatic informative systems containing all information on the networks as well as of the consumptions of the users and at the same time the knowledge of the typical load curves makes load flow calculations easier in statistical terms. This allows design of an enhanced calculation methodology to be used to check the compliance with the technical constraints in probabilistic terms. This is of paramount importance when considering distribution networks, particularly at the LV level, where, due to the reduced number of users connected to each feeder, the statistical effects could prove relevant for selecting the best size of network components. Although for MV networks real time feeder current measurements are generally available from SCADA systems, nevertheless it can prove very useful to have at disposal software tools allowing calculation of the values of currents, voltage drops and losses on each branch of the network. With better reason, this is important for LV networks, where, generally, automatic and systematic measurements are not available. The statistical method for load flow calculation in radial distribution systems described can be used both with reference to the present load condition (operation) and for the future load forecasted on the nodes of the network (planning studies). Although the validity of this approach is quite general, in this paper its applications for LV systems (three phases and neutral wire) is particularly emphasised.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of the location of defects accessible from an MV network control system (SCADA)
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Usine d'Electricite de Metz (France) is currently involved in a vast telecontrol project for its high and medium voltage power networks. The originality of the operation lies in the overall approach to the problem, with the integration, during requirement analyses, of aspects relating to telecontrol, control support and maintenance, service quality management and network scheduling, so as to ensure that the information system will have maximum coherence and pertinence. The connection of oscilloperturbographs to the telecontrol system was envisaged during the functional study of control support (SCADA/DMS).

articleTitle: A new solution of 150 kV overhead compact line
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: In countries, such as Italy, characterised by the intensive use of land for various purposes (industrial, agricultural, residential), the construction of overhead lines is increasingly constrained due to the growing awareness of the population towards environmental issues and the passing of special laws for the safeguard of environmental assets. The current community approach in the field of environmental protection calls for the adoption of technical planning and decision-making processes that make it possible to assess the impact of works and constructions on the environment in advance, during the study and design phase. In order to meet these needs, ENEL is experimenting new advanced solutions to make overhead lines more compact that have been developed in relation to the actual application on the field. One of these solutions, used for the reconstruction of a line in the outskirts of Rome, is described. The solution is based on the use of poles and bored pile foundations.

articleTitle: STEP-standard as a means to document electrotechnical installations in the distribution system?
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Since machinery and equipment used for operation in electric utility companies is generally employed for many decades, documentation is required which can be used across the equipment's entire service life. Such documentation has to contain all pertinent information and must be accessible within a reasonable period of time. Since most of the machinery and equipment used for operation in power distribution networks is standardised and since ensuring the required flow of information is, in many cases, a major cost factor, it is quite interesting to consider this flow of technical information not just within the confines of one's own company (i.e. the utility company). While a number of industrial sectors already have their respective technical STEP standards, the technical standard for the field of electrical engineering, the application protocol (AP) 212 (ISO 10303-212), is currently still being drafted. However, the experience gained in the development and use of STEP-AP in other industries leads to the assumption that the STEP standard may also gain considerable importance for utility company users of electrical products.

articleTitle: Development of a diagnostic system for noncontinuously operating machines
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: A portable, computer based, time domain diagnostic system has been developed, including hardware and software. Accurate measurement of machine timing and fault simulation has been demonstrated. The method has much to offer in terms of providing a noninvasive method for obtaining knowledge of the operational state of a machine, such as a diverter switch from a transformer load tap changer, and provides possibilities for use in future programmed maintenance schedules. Data collection and analysis methods are given.

articleTitle: Eliminating fault-induced voltage sags at an industrial plant: a comparative evaluation of solutions
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Sensitive electrical equipment in industrial facilities can be shut down suddenly by voltage sags. The tolerance of these devices to deviations in the magnitude of the supply voltage varies, but the most sensitive equipment often is critical to operations. This paper describes the results of a study that assessed methods for reducing the impact of voltage sags on an industrial plant power system. The study investigated several methods for reducing the depth of sags by modifying the electric utility and industrial power distribution systems. The study emphasized conventional methods of improving this aspect of power quality through system modifications, and especially on finding the most cost-effective methods. A sliding-fault method was used to determine the effectiveness of specific mitigation solutions.

articleTitle: The technical and economic case for the use of three dimensional mapping for the installation of electric power cables
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The paper reviews the experimental work carried out by MEB on the practical usage of three dimensional mapping. Evidence is provided to show how the technique has proved to be an effective pre-planning tool which has significantly reduced cable installation costs and increased the use of trenchless technology. The technique involves using electromagnetic locators and then ground based radar.

articleTitle: Results of the evaluation campaign carried out by ENEL on the performances of electric heat pumps for room climatisation in residential and tertiary sectors
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: ENEL is looking at the diffusion of electric technologies as a basic tool for improving efficiency in end energy uses, in conformity with the engagements taken on with public control authority as concerns rational and environment-friendly energy use. An intensive research programme was started, which consisted of in-depth technological analyses on types of apparatus available on the Italian market. The objectives of such researches comprise, among others: measurement of energy performances coefficients obtained during seasonal working, and comparison with the values measured in the laboratory in ideal conditions and with the catalogue data declared by constructors; evaluation of primary energy savings obtainable through the electric heat pump, compared with other climatisation apparatus fuelled with fossil fuels (boiler, heat pump operated by a gas engine and absorption refrigerator); and identification of the national territory areas where local climate conditions allow the utilisation of a heat pump for winter heating with no need for additional heat generators. This report expounds the whole of tests and measurements in progress separately for both of the mentioned use sectors; also whenever possible the results already available when the report was drawn up are specified.

articleTitle: An efficient technique for determining contact voltages and grounding resistances in multi-stratum land, for standardised transforming centres
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: As a preliminary step before design of the grounding installation for a transforming centre, the terrain is surveyed by means of vertical electric sounding, usually using F. Wenner's method. When the results are interpreted in order to predict stratigraphy, it is normal to find that the model corresponds to that of a multi-stratum terrain. In general, a minimum of two and a maximum of six strata are found. Very rarely, the terrain is modellable as homogenous. However, as is well known, there is at present no efficient procedure which enables the contact voltage and grounding diffusion resistance to be obtained quickly and precisely for electrodes with a complex geometry in the case of multi-stratum terrain types. As part of its new standardisation plan for transforming centres of up to 20 kV, 2/spl times/630 KVA (MTDYC Standards), and their corresponding grounding points, Iberdrola has developed a procedure to determine, with extraordinary efficiency, the contact voltage and grounding resistance in all standardised transforming centres, whatever the structure of the terrain (two to six strata) where they are to be located. The technique is applicable to grounding points for transforming centres of the following types: all-weather post; all-weather compact; surface prefabricated; and underground. The purpose of this paper is to present the procedure used, based on a technique of reduction inspired by the equipotential surfaces method, combined with an adjustment technique which uses the function /spl chi//sup 2/, and utilises exponential, parabolic hyperbolic and where necessary, linear functions.

articleTitle: Distance protection of asymmetrical overhead lines
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Distance protection is based on the measurement of the impedance of power system short-circuit loops and the comparison with given settings. Conversion of the measured short-circuit impedances using kilometric impedance values allows distances to be evaluated. In any case, an ideally symmetrical line structure is assumed. In practice, however, such an ideal symmetry cannot be reached for overhead power lines, even if transposed. Complete transposition of an overhead line, for instance, is effective only in case of a short-circuit at the end of the line. Today, overhead lines often are not transposed to reduce costs. This paper shows how asymmetries of single- and double-circuit power lines can be taken into account when fault distances are determined using various compensation methods. The asymmetry is directly included in the process of modeling of the distance protection.

articleTitle: INTFO: corporation integrated multimedia intelligent assistant for field operators. An overview [power system control]
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The INTFO project aims at developing a flexible multimedia application running cooperatively on corporate information systems and on portable (mobile) personal computers to organize and improve the efficiency of power system operators performing every-day activities in the field. It will help: electric utility company operation managers to organise and distribute the necessary tasks between the operators; and field operators by providing guidance and assistance in the inspection, maintenance, operation and modification of equipment, using multimedia (voice register, photographs), geographic and alphanumeric data and procedures.

articleTitle: The effects of material management on the reliability of an electricity distribution network and modeling the logistic system for fault situations
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Deregulation, opening markets and new business minded owners are placing more and more pressure on electricity distribution utilities to be cost-effective. Lappeenranta University of Technology has, together with a group of Finnish electricity distribution utilities, conducted a cost-effectiveness study of a logistics system for rural distribution networks. This study has examined an optimized logistic system, the personnel and the equipment needed in a fault situation. This paper models the dependence between material management and the reliability of electricity distribution networks. The aim is to find a solution that will result in the minimum total costs, including the costs of outages, storage, material in storage, personnel and equipment needed in the power system repair process.

articleTitle: Real experience in the connection of wind power production in distribution network
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: For the implantation of the wind farm at the El Perdon site, numerous measurements were made of wind direction and speed. These measurements made it possible to predict a high number of hours of operation annually and an important energy production. Moreover, it was necessary to determine the ideal connection point to the network that would guarantee the removal (evacuation) of the energy produced and to study the impact of the wind farm in order to preserve the supply quality parameters already set by IBERDROLA. Finally, the results of real operation and the measurements carried out are shown, to prove that the voltage and frequency quality are as forecast.

articleTitle: Benefits of distribution automation and performance results from a network trial
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Typical medium voltage distribution systems have developed slowly over many years and essentially comprise of circuit breakers at primary substations feeding a series of isolatable step-down transformers. Customers have been demanding better continuity of supply and performance from the power network and electric utilities have been investigating ways of responding without the need for large capital investment. Improvements in switching devices, protection relays and telecontrol in recent years have made the implementation of distribution automation schemes cost-effective and the benefits are being realised through a number of installations. This paper explores the benefits of distribution automation, details the equipment required and raises a number of issues relating to a real installation.

articleTitle: Connectors for power cables. Experience of testing according to new standard IEC 1238-1
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Throughout the world there has been a number of national standards for testing connectors for power cables. The different test methods made it very difficult to introduce new connection systems into new markets. There was a need for an international standard, and the work started as early as 1976. As an input for the work several national standards were used. The work was very difficult, which is reflected in the fact that it took until 1993 before IEC 1238-1 was published. The end result is a standard which in principle follows the traditional method of heat cycling for accelerated ageing. Requirements and statistical evaluation of the test values are influenced by existing national standards. An attempt was made to introduce a more scientific method developed by the former ECRC in Capenhurst, UK, for both ageing and assessing of the test results. The method was not accepted because of unfamiliarity with the method and the work-load that was needed to correlate this test method with existing methods. Many countries were using the VDE standard as it was, or with minor modifications. In our comparisons we refer to the old VDE standard for crimp connections. A separate VDE standard for mechanical connections is also available.

articleTitle: Contribution to the determination of the basic load proportion of noncentralised, regenerative power generation plants in the supply area of a regional power supplier
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Under the German law on energy supply, the Energieversorgung Suedsachsen AG (EVS AG) as a regional supplier with more than half a million customers for both tariff and special contractual conditions, and presupplier to 12 urban plants with a maximum mains supply of more than 920 MW has the obligation to collect and enrich energy which was generated by noncentralised, regenerative power sources. Within the framework of wind measurement programmes, a possible extension of about 360 MW was determined for the supply area of the EVS AG. Based on new developments on the wind power plant market with the clear trend to the erection of wind power plants in the country, this value seems to be feasible in the future. For water power stations, a possible, installed, total capacity of about 40 MW with an increase to come mainly from the extension of formerly shut-down plants is assumed for the future. Feeding by photovoltaic plants is not a relevant scale. In October 1996, the installed capacity of wind power plants amounted to about 34 MW, and of water power plants, to 35 MW. Since the EVS AG does not have independent generating plants, and receives the entire capacity from presuppliers, it is becoming necessary to assess the capacity potentials of noncentralised, regenerative power sources in order to obtain an information on the sum of the monthly guaranteed proportions. The quantity of the energy which is made available by regenerative energy sources at a certain time cannot be ascertained in a deterministic way. The problems arising from an offer-dependent supply can only be dealt with by methods of probability calculus.

articleTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition On Electricity Distribution - CIRED - Part 1: Contributions
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of industrial power networks considering production plants
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Methods for the probabilistic calculation of power network reliability predominantly assess the occurrence of interruptions of supply at individual nodes. This approach proves to be too coarse for the planning of industrial power networks, for which specific requirements of individual production plant also have to be taken into account. The following article demonstrates a methodology with which these requirements, and the behavior of complex production processes in case of network failures, can be included in the power network reliability analysis. The results which can be achieved with these and which assess the reliability with reference to the production outages are presented for the example of a selected case study.

articleTitle: Power interruptions-key figures and filtering of statistical data
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: This paper addresses several topics regarding the Norwegian power quality strategy. It gives a brief presentation of the FASIT system, how calculation and reporting of key figures based on the registrations are carried out, and a presentation of preliminary results from the first year with reported key figures (1995). The problem of large standard deviations in reported key figures from one year to another is also addressed in the paper. Finally, the last section outlines the Norwegian power quality strategy (status and future aims/plans).

articleTitle: Guide for assessing the network harmonic impedance
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The objective of this report is to provide practical guidance for assessing power system harmonic impedance, taking into account the considered network voltage (LV, MV or HV), the disturbing load importance (small or great contribution to the power network pollution) and the analytical and computational tools available.

articleTitle: Lightning protection of distribution networks. II. Application to MV networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: For pt. I see Proc. CIRED, Birmingham, UK, IEE (1997). The basic information for designers of lightning protection of MV and LV networks is given in part I. Part II gives an application of this basic information to the lightning protection of MV networks containing overhead lines. As the overvoltages due to lightning reach important values, an economical and safe network design calls for extensive lightning protection. This general statement applies to high voltage as well as medium and low voltage networks. Overvoltage protection can be basically achieved in two ways: reducing the amplitude and rate of occurrence of lightning overvoltages at the point of origin (e.g. through shielding the line conductors or improving the footing resistance of towers); and limiting the overvoltage at the equipment location (e.g. through surge arresters). In high voltage networks, both methods of protection are common. In MV networks shielding the conductors is generally not very effective. Due to the small clearance between the earth wire and the conductors, a direct lightning stroke will usually hit the conductors as well. In addition, induced overvoltages can be reduced only to a low extent by shield wires, as reported in part I. For these reasons, the most effective protection against overvoltages in such networks is the use of surge arresters or spark gaps in the vicinity of the equipment. The paper gives guidance in the selection of rating and position of such protective devices and gives some indication on the effect of their use on the quality of the supply.

articleTitle: High standards for modern HV power cable system environments
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Privatisation of the Electricity Supply Industry (ESI) in the UK has brought with it a number of changes, increasing the expectations of electricity customers and Regional Electricity Companies (RECs) for the economic provision of enhanced system reliability, guarantees of electricity supply, reduced maintenance and increased awareness of the environment. New national legislation legally enforces the obligation of RECs to protect the environment and raise standards in the specification, manufacture, installation and operation of power cable networks. Success in setting higher standards for HV (33-132 kV) power cables, at reasonable cost, is being achieved by establishing joint initiatives between RECs and cable manufacturers. Working together, cable system life spans can be extended and security of supply enhanced to the benefit of their customers and the environment. More mechanically robust cable system designs are being made available, to combat an increasing tendency to damage by third parties, e.g. other utilities, with a greater emphasis on solid designs, extruded metallic sheaths and medium density polyethylene (MDPE) oversheaths. With available land for new HV feeder routes becoming more scarce, it is increasingly important to reduce 'rights of way' by selecting cables of a smaller size and longer drum length, and to consider carefully the installation design and after-laying tests.

articleTitle: Internal faults in distribution switchgear-modelling, implementation and testing of new switchgear designs
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The internal fault qualification of new distribution switchgear designs is well established internationally. Different manufacturers have responded in various ways to achieve the required performance. This paper presents one manufacturer's approach in respect of modelling, design and testing. The requirements of national codes and international standards are also considered.

articleTitle: Upgrades to remote-control systems at EDF GDF services
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: EDF is upgrading its distribution network remote control systems. By the end of 1997, three centres run by EDF GDF Services (in Paris, Lyon and Versailles) will be equipped with a Siemens SCADA system. A number of functions developed by EDF as part of work on the Austral project (event reporting, diagnostics, service resumption assistance, etc.) will then be implemented on the SCADAs at Lyon and Versailles. At the same time, an alternative upgrade solution is being investigated for the 75 computerized remote control systems (CRSs) developed by EDF around 1980. In December 1996, EDF started experimentation on a new prototype SCADA at the Nimes centre. For this prototype, the existing real-time CRS software, with all its functionalities, was ported onto a Unix workstation. High-reliability communication with the primary substations is provided by a meshed X25 transmission network and all data on primary substations and the medium-voltage grid is managed by a new configurator. To facilitate incident analysis, an off-the-shelf user interface will provide graphic representations of the grid in different degrees of detail: with dynamic colour coding of feeders. The new architecture for the prototype SCADA implements object-oriented data modelling of the grid components. Application modules-developed by EDF (e.g. Austral functions) or third-party manufacturers (e.g. user interface with dynamic colour-coding of grid features)-will then be able to access this data much more easily than they did on the previous architectures, which used remote procedure calls. This new approach will be one of the first practical applications of recent EPRI and IEC work on open upgradeable remote control systems.

articleTitle: Wear of conductor support fittings
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The report gives a survey of component failures, variation in the wear of line fittings along overhead lines, the influence of the operating condition on wear and available operation strength of the fitting. Wear is a time-dependent deterioration which is possible to detect and assess under development, and further it seems to be possible to point out the most probable sites for wear of conductor support fittings.

articleTitle: SISPIR: an integrated system for multi-stage investment plan selection and scheduling in an electric distribution network
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The selection, for a later development, of an important set of investments between the total set of investment opportunities from an electric utility company in front of all kind of limitations that can exist in it, presents a great complexity decision problem, difficult to solve with success without the help of as much the necessary financial knowledge, as the adequate operational research techniques. Complexity is pointed, on one hand by diversity related to nature, value and risk of investments which compete for the same resources, and on the other by the variety of existent limitations for its realization. The decision process, faced with an enough number of investment possibilities, unavoidably finalizes in an investment planning which takes into account as much the mutual characteristics of each one of the candidate investments as the interactions between them and any other limitation which could exist, obliged or due to company policy.

articleTitle: eaNSF: a simulation tool for evaluating strategies
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: EA Technology's Network Simulation Facility, eaNSF, has been developed for the Regional Electricity Companies as a PC program to provide a common basis for the economic and strategic evaluation of commercial and technical developments which depend intrinsically upon the capability or performance of the distribution network. Such developments may be phased over a period of years and need to be considered along with various scenarios for load growth, tariff rates and structures. The changes may be for example: the effect of capturing or introducing new loads; changing or omitting voltage levels; replacing equipment to give improvements in performance or to reduce energy losses; introducing different protection policies; reliability assessment etc. Each evaluation requires an appropriate representation of the network along with the ability to analyse its performance under different loads and a means of linking performance with short and long term costs. It is essential when comparing different options, that evaluations are carried out on a consistent basis where the assumptions are explicit and matched to the particular requirements of each company.

articleTitle: Customer account management system for STEWEAG key accounts
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The liberalisation (de-regulation) of the energy markets creates a new environment, with new requirements and demands on electric utilities and their business practices. STEWEAG (Austria) responded to these changes of the market by initiating an in-depth re-engineering process for the whole company in 1993. This re-engineering was mainly focused towards customer orientation, flat and flexible organisational structures, fast and correct answers to customer demands and increased transparency of processes. The customer account (billing) management system for industrial and commercial customers is to be regarded as part of this process of re-engineering.

articleTitle: The seven services which EDF provides to small and medium-sized companies
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The company's approach to small and medium-sized businesses is part of EDF's strategy of building a modern public service. This involves: paying closer attention to customers and members of the public, listening to their opinions and acting accordingly; providing all customers with a standard of service giving the highest level of quality in Europe combined with the best price, and to guarantee a first class service at competitive rates throughout the country; and offering all customers ranges of additional services to satisfy their specific expectations. The seven services provide a response to three areas of concern: making electricity management easier and controlling costs; controlling electrical processes; and guaranteeing the quality of the electricity supplied to the customer. The seven services are: DIAPASON, applying the most suitable tariff at points of delivery; FACILIS, customized payment facilities; ELECTRO PROCESS, information on processes and assistance in training on processes; EMERAUDE, contractual commitment concerning the quality of supply and detailing maximum power cut limits; ECHO RESEAU, information for a new consumer on the quality of the electrical supply to be provided; PREVENANCE, information on planned power cuts; and FIABELEC, a complete solution to reducing the sensitivity of an internal electrical installation.

articleTitle: Flicker prediction and simulation in public and industrial systems
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Today, the prediction and limitation planning of power system flicker is of increasing importance. In medium voltage networks for example, the number of wind generators is rapidly increasing, showing high power fluctuation and resulting in flicker problems. In the low voltage networks of industrial installations especially, spot welding machines necessitate the prediction and planning of the voltage quality. It has been found that classical load flow simulations are time consuming and lead to unrealistic results. A new fast simulation method has been developed, enabling the simulation of power systems with a high number of rapidly fluctuating loads and stochastic generators such as wind generators. The stochastic behaviour of loads and generators is simulated by a scenario generator. The distribution network can be simulated either as a single- or three-phase system. The result of simulation is a voltage time profile of the network. With the help of integrated software, the full function of a flickermeter for the evaluation of the flicker level is possible. The system has been successfully tested for an industrial power system with spot welding machines. In future, it will be used for the planning of the power quality of new Austrian wind farms and industrial factory installations with numerous welding robots.

articleTitle: Achieving energy efficiency in restructured markets, implications for IRP
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The shift of the focus of the vertically integrated model to the new unbundled models of organization to attain a "new competitive" Electricity Supply Industry brings new subjects into integrated resource planning (IRP) study. The centralized decisions on new capacity additions is being substituted by market mechanisms, changing the implementation of the IRP regarding both the construction of new capacity and the demand side management (DSM). The implication for DSM is that, without a central planning process, it will not be possible to carry out IRP. It would be necessary to intervene in the market to introduce mechanisms to encourage investment decisions in favour of energy efficiency programmes where they are economically feasible. Some countries are implementing policies tending to create a more favorable attitude towards energy efficiency in products and services. The conventional programmes of demand-side management are being redesigned as added-value services to conserve or create market quota through market transformation mechanisms, such as technology procurement.

articleTitle: Activities of AEDC for a reliable service with relation to users
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Alexandria Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC) serves about 1.2 million consumers on the medium voltage and low voltage. This network is fed from 22 substations with a total installed capacity of 2000 MVA. The components of the network include: 127 medium voltage switch boards, 6060 km medium voltage cables, 10690 km low voltage overhead and underground cables and 4310 distribution transformers. The total annual sale amounts to 3420 M.kWH. To secure a high degree of reliability for the customer service and to meet the receiving large load growth, AEDC conducted a rehabilitation plan to the distribution network. To meet the requirements of the user, AEDC undertook some activities such as: technical support-periodical technical inspections of the installations at the user side to improve the service reliability; energy conservation-installation of capacitor banks at the end user and at the network to improve the power factor and also installation of energy efficient lighting systems; and power quality-measurements were carried out for industrial, commercial and residential loads in detecting the existing level of the power quality. This paper presents the results of measurements for power quality: harmonics, voltage variation and remedies. Also the recommendations remedies which were carried out are stated.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the sealing system and of the electric performance of the distribution lightning arresters
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: After certifying the unsatisfactory performance of the lightning arresters and identifying the moisture penetration as the main cause, a methodology for the sealing evaluation of such lightning arresters was researched and developed. Moreover, the electric conditions of the lightning arresters in the manufacturing line and in the stocks of concessionaires (new ones) were verified and still those taken out of operation in networks and by operation of the automatic disconnector or internal criteria of the concessionaires (used ones).

articleTitle: The new system and installation of the optical phase conductor on 15 kV lines in Poland
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The dynamic development of the optical telecommunication system (OTS) observed in Poland in recent years has been possible due to application of various methods for installation of optical fibre cables on power supply lines. The market in the past has been dominated by optical ground wire (OPGW). The reason for this is that a majority of optical cable lines are installed at the time of line repairs, replacing old ground wires with OPGW. This technology has been used for 220 kV and 400 kV lines. The information given in this paper clarifies the circumstances of, and conditions for, constructing the first Polish telecommunication optical cable line on 15 kV lines using the optical phase conductor (OPCON).

articleTitle: Increasing the availability of the medium voltage network in the Netherlands
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The electricity supply in the Netherlands, to an average domestic customer, can be considered to be one of the most reliable of the world. As an average, every 5 years a customer will be confronted with a failure in the public electricity supply system. On an annual basis, this results in an outage time of less than 20 minutes. Because approximately 15 minutes of the above mentioned outage time is due to faults in the medium voltage network, it is obvious to concentrate on medium voltage when one wishes to increase power system availability. In this paper, a relatively simple and economical solution is discussed to increase the availability of the MV power network. It is based on the remote reading of (self-resetting) short-circuit indicators in the power network. After a description of the functionality and use of the indicator itself, the paper concentrates on the remote reading and its impact on the availability of the network. It is shown that considerable search time can be saved in faulty situations, by almost immediate knowing the failure's location in the power network.

articleTitle: Comparison of fault management applications in French and Finnish distribution control centers
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: This paper compares two systems providing advanced functions for real-time management of power distribution networks developed in Finland and in France. The overall aim of these systems is to minimize the operational costs (e.g. power losses, outage costs) subject to the technical constraints (e.g. voltage level, thermal limits). These are to be integrated with a supervision control acquisition system (SCADA) and heterogeneous databases such as network and geographical information systems (AM/FM/GIS). In this paper, the authors briefly introduce both systems and discuss their similarities and differences in more detail. The main focus is on the systems' connection to SCADA and fault management functions but both systems provide other functionalities beyond the scope of the present paper.

articleTitle: Results of the project on service quality in the Eastern region of Spain
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: This paper seeks to offer an overall view of the most significant results obtained once that the research project entitled "Study of short time interruptions in the Spanish electrical network and of methods to minimise their effects" has terminated. This project was carried out within the Electrotechnical Research and Development Programme of OCIDE (PIE no. 132219), that IBERDROLA, in collaboration with the GEDEE Research Group of the Electrical Engineering Department of the Polytechnic University of Valencia and the company UITESA, carried out between 1991 and 1995. This paper focuses on: the aspects related to the incidence of conducted electrical disturbances on clients; the systematics followed to propose solutions; the economic evaluation of these incidents; and the recommendations made on the electricity supply quality.

articleTitle: CEANDER cable for low tension underground distribution. Special tests
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: In order to unify and improve the benefits of low tension distribution cables and the service which the electrical companies are offering their customers, in July of 1993 the "GT de Averias de UNESA" (the GT UNESA Breakdowns), decided to undertake the matter together with the cable manufacturers. The mixed UNESA-FACEL Work Group was created in order to evaluate the different distribution cable designs at 0.6/1 kV, both technically and economically. Both the unipolar cables, the ones which are most commonly used in Spain, as well as the multipolar cable (Districable-France, CEANDER-Switzerland/Italy, etc.), used in most of the EEC countries were analysed. With the new CEANDER for low tension distribution (0.6/1 kV) and in order to have an experimental data base available, regarding the behaviour of the cable in critical service conditions, a series of special tests were carried out, at the request of IBERDROLA and ENDESA, which are detailed in this paper: short-circuit tests (25 cycles/15 s at 1700 A and 2000 A); overload tests (3 h at 504 A and 640 A); magnetic field measurement in a laboratory; and magnetic field measuring in a real installation.

articleTitle: Strategy for the renewal of 110 kV substations
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Under the impression that there would be high load increases and the target levels of service reliability should be ensured, the German utility Hamburgische Electricitats-Werke AG (HEW) of the city-state of Hamburg constructed a large number of 110 kV substations between 1950 and 1970. Given the specific age structure of the substations and the current state of the electrical equipment in use, HEW has taken advantage of the planned renewal of a large 110 kV substation to develop a strategic approach to the timely evaluation of existing high-voltage plant which also allows long-term maintenance measures to be planned. Future refits will be largely influenced by revised considerations of the company's philosophy on service reliability, by the inclusion of long-term load forecasts, and by an integrated rolling planning system for the entire 110 kV distribution network. In view of the expected changes and greater competition on the international electrical energy market, the remaining life time of system equipment must be exploited more strongly in order to reduce high investments for the necessary functional substance conservation of the high-voltage power system.

articleTitle: Evaluating and assessing a necessary generation change in network control systems
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: As a result of the rapidly advancing computer and communications technologies, a major technological shift is expected to take place within the next 5 to 10 years. Among other benefits, it will then be possible for one and the same digital network to be used for voice communication, data exchange and office communications. As a result, the cost of operating a power systems will be reduced considerably. Standardized interfaces and protocols will allow the computer system to be connected to the data network. Companies will increasingly aim at centralizing all data acquisition and maintenance work so as to eventually be able to eliminate redundant data maintenance activities previously performed on different computers. The introduction of open-system capabilities in the mainframe computer system, as a first step in the upgrading process, would allow the power system to be monitored from remote locations. Malfunction and switching-state information would be transmitted in the form text messages. In a second step, graphical representation of the power system's operating status and even functions allowing network elements to be controlled in the graphics mode could be implemented. This would require a high-capacity data network and appropriate means of ensuring clear identification of transmitting and receiving stations. The power system could then be operated in two rather than three shifts. A stand-by crew on night duty could receive relevant information via a data line, allowing costs to be reduced even further. More importantly, the physical and psychological strain currently placed on the operating staff by their three-shift work will be eased, thus humanizing their working conditions without compromising system security.

articleTitle: Active control system of the energy in low voltage distribution networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: This paper presents the development and results obtained from an active control system of the energy in low-voltage networks subjected to disturbances, and in which the maintenance of the anticipated voltage margins is an important factor.
