This system, due to its good performance in a dynamic regime, is a rapid voltage stabiliser that insulates the network from disturbances caused by nonlinear charges, allows for reactive energy and harmonic control, and de-sensitises the load during short-term voltage sags. At the same time, it permits the automatic programming of the output voltage value in order to save energy.

articleTitle: A comparison between DC and AC drives as regards their behaviour in the presence of voltage dips: new techniques for reducing the susceptibility of AC drives
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Electrical adjustable speed drives are sensitive to voltage interruptions. The occurrence of voltage dips in the power supply to pieces of equipment may cause them to stall, and cause production losses. Here, an examination is made of the behaviour in the presence of voltage dips in supplies for thyristor controlled DC drives, and of different kinds of AC drives. A discussion on AC equipment sensitivity attenuating techniques, and on the options which manufacturers incorporate into their equipment in order to minimize that sensitivity is presented. A a description of the strategy used at the MEP (Spain) for the purpose of examining the cases brought in by customers whose equipment is affected by the voltage dips is also detailed. There are details on two cases that were examined, plus the suggested proposals for their solution. The paper is based on studies that have been conducted by MEP in conjunction with IBERDROLA, as were developed under the Electro-Technical Research Plan financed by Spain's electric power utilities, with coordination by the Electro-Technical Research Coordination Office (OCIDE).

articleTitle: Amorphous core transformers: behaviour in particular network conditions and design comparisons
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: This report aims at enhancing market acceptance of amorphous core distribution transformers (AMDT) in Europe. PAUWELS TRAFO built several prototypes and trial series, supported by ELECTRABEL in its "Rational Use of Energy" effort. Several units were tested at the laboratories of LABORELEC.

articleTitle: New terminations for distribution-class shielded power cables
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Cable terminations are installed over prepared shielded power cables where a portion of the insulation shield has been removed. The functions of a typical termination are to provide a cable end seal, electrical stress control, and external insulation covering. Sealing the end of solid dielectric power cables is important to prevent water from entering the power cable and degrading the cable insulation. Electrical stress control is needed to prevent a dielectric breakdown at the end of the insulation shield in both the air and cable insulation. An insulation covering must limit leakage current and resist both tracking and erosion from exposure to the environmental conditions in a strong electric field. The ultimate performance and reliability of a termination depends on its materials, design, installation and operating environment. New materials and design were required to achieve the target improvements. A new termination with tapered two-component capacitive stress-control, track-resistant silicone and cold-shrink delivery system was developed. The paper describes the materials, design and performance results for these new terminations.

articleTitle: Improving supply reliability for Southern Electric's rural customers
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Market research carried out on behalf of Southern Electric has shown that customers find short duration interruptions, typically less than half a minute, just as inconvenient as longer ones. The decision was taken to improve reliability for rural customers and to make key sections of the overhead network as reliable as the underground ones. The majority, around 75%, of 'customer minutes lost' occur as a result of faults on the 11 kV overhead network. After surveying a sample of lines the decision was taken to rebuild the worst performing with insulated conductor. This would address all the causes apart from lightning and therefore significantly improve customer service. The author discusses this rebuilding programme.

articleTitle: MV network control integrated on the SCADA system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: LTE-the Portuguese electric utility-has proceeded with an MV power system (30 kV and 10 kV) control scheme , according to a company strategy defined on the bases of better service quality provision to its clients and minimisation of interruption time. Using the present SCADA systems, open systems, integrated into a global information network, in corporation with other systems and with DMS applications (distribution management system), it was considered fundamental that the MV power network control should be integrated on the existing SCADA scheme in the distribution centres (DC). For the choice of the points on the network to be controlled, the authors have considered the network characteristics, the installed power, the type and number of clients, incident quantification, etc., for the determination of the most favourable technical/economical solution. As a communication support, they used several solutions, such as radio, dedicated telephone lines, commuted telephone lines or distribution line carriers (DLC), that aid the network control system in the command centre, and determine the location of the incident and isolate the affected network.

articleTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)

articleTitle: A new technical step in underground links for 90 kV high voltage energy transportation
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Since 1962, synthetic insulated power cables have been used in France for 63 and 90 kV networks, with over 700 km of links already in service and with excellent outcome of experience. This is in particular due to a qualification test procedure of the complete cable system plus accessories which ensures the intrinsic quality of the components and their perfect compatibility. Many evolutions have taken place in thirty years and, since 1987, the only material used for HV cable insulation has been cross-linked polyethylene. The new 90 kV power cable advances one step further, with a new reduction of insulation thickness and the use of aluminium screens. Innovation also includes the development of new accessories, with in particular, "one piece-premoulded" joints and synthetic material terminations. Simultaneously, from the experience acquired in medium voltage applications, a mechanized technique for high voltage link laying has been developed and validated, first in the laboratory, and then on the power network.

articleTitle: Deregulation-challenges and impacts for planning and documentation
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: In a deregulated electricity distribution the network business and energy business are separated from each other. Free competition exists in the energy business but the network business will still at least temporarily remain monopolistic and regulated by a government authority ("regulator"). An essential feature of the transfer tariff in distribution networks is that it is independent of the distance. This development has taken place e.g. in Norway, Finland and Sweden and it has created new challenges also for planning and documentation. Also transmission networks are now open for any trader.

articleTitle: Combined heat and power production. Industrial development
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Thanks to the latest modifications of reglementations, economic and industrial perspectives, and thanks to the improvement of technology, combined heat and power production is expanding in most industrialized (or on the way to be industrialized) countries. According to this general evolution and to the European Union instructions for liberation of power production, the French market of CHP production is growing. Specific technical problems are created by generators which are continually connected to existing production, distribution and users systems. These problems are listed in this paper where GEC ALSTHOM provides industrial solutions.

articleTitle: Application of neural networks for load forecasting in a regional power company
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The supervision of purchases from power generators is, for each regional power company (RPC), an important economy measure. A prerequisite for this measure is to have knowledge of short-term load development in the area to be supplied. In an automated load forecasting system, the accuracy of the forecasts is increased in order to give the experienced RPC a better safety margin in critical decision-making situations. This can only be achieved when the factors influencing the load are taken into account. Furthermore, an automated load forecasting system, which consists of hardware and software components, must be capable of being integrated in a functional manner into the existing grid control and load control system of the RPC, in order to achieve a successful upgrade. An upgrade, because of its lower cost when compared to a self-contained system which has its own process control, is especially suitable for local and regional power companies.

articleTitle: Saving the environment and saving costs: drives for continous improvements of NKF LV cable production
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: LCA (life cycle analysis) of distribution cables has been presented to utilities and cablemakers. Two major items of environmental impact are: energy loss (I/sup 2/R), while using the cable, and refining metals for the conductors. Multilateral discussions between utilities, KEMA and cablemakers in the Netherlands now pay attention to the first item. The second point has resulted in a drive for technological developments at NKF. Three technological developments were started: recycling of PVC scrap; improving the silane process for LV XLPE; and insulation skin colour coding.

articleTitle: Pressure stress of switchgear and compact substations in case of internal arcs
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The internal arc tests of compact substations to prove the safety of personnel in case of internal arcs can be divided in two separate tests if there are maximum permitted values of pressure stress in the different compartments. To ensure that the pressure stress is lower than the pressure withstand capability, pressure relief devices and pressure reducing means are necessary. Under these conditions, the pressure withstand capability of the housing of the compact substation and the incorporated medium voltage switchgear can be tested with simplified, minor expensive tests. However, tests to prove the impact of hot arc gases requires tests under real conditions.

articleTitle: An integrated solution for safety and reliability on rural distribution networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Customer minutes lost per year is becoming a critically important criterion by which electrical supply companies are judged. Continuity of supply is playing an increasingly important part in everyday life, and has generally raised the user's expectation of the quality of supply. Electronic equipment, particularly computers, are reliant upon an uninterrupted power supply. Previously unnoticeable power interruptions are now highlighted to the user and can result in problems. In order to minimise the potential problems, a review of the quality of supply provided by the electricity supply companies has taken place. The Electricity Supply Regulator decreed that customer minutes lost are restricted to a prescribed figure. This has resulted in electricity supply companies reviewing their networks and has culminated in various schemes being devised in order to improve the quality of supply provided. One of these is an overhead distribution network with an insulated overhead line as the main backbone of the system, having uninsulated lines feeding consumers to maximise the benefit ratio. This paper describes equipment designed to operate on such a network including the LINX pole mounted auto-isolating recloser which consists of: vacuum interrupters; bushings; actuator; operations counter; relay; and batteries.

articleTitle: Optimization in the application of reclosers
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: At present, CESP has 548 pole-type recloser units in its 13.8 kV and 34.5 kV distribution system, acquired within a period of 20 years. Annually, with the LDs (distribution line) and LDRs (rural distribution line) extensions to attend new connections and/or strengthen the distribution system, in some conditions there is an increase of temporary failures influenced, for instance, by the high Keraunic level of some regions, that make it feasible the installation of reclosers through the increase in operational cost of the system and in the cost of electric energy supply. On the other hand, with the alterations made in the power system configurations and adequate cleaning of LDs stretch, some lines show no longer the need of a recloser due to few well succeeded automatic operations. Based on this fact, and because of the availability operation data (data bank of interruptions, recloser performance file, etc.) it was possible to systematically rationalize the reclosers use in the distribution system of CESP.

articleTitle: A software based design methodology for the design of low-cost electrical reticulation networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: In South Africa, the challenge of the early 21st Century is to extend the supply of grid electricity to many of the currently unelectrified urban and rural households. As part of the recently elected government's reconstruction and development plan, the intention is to electrify 500,000 households per year for the next 10 to 15 years. This paper describes a research and development project being undertaken at the University of the Witwatersrand, in Johannesburg, aimed at providing the designers of electrical distribution networks with an integrated set of software tools.

articleTitle: New ways of influencing customers ~electric utility stategies\
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The Danish utility NESA wants to profile itself towards its customers. In Denmark, only a handful of the largest customers-one of which is located in NESA's supply area-have been given the freedom to choose their electricity supplier by themselves, but everybody expects the number of customers on the free market to increase in the nearer future. Everybody is preparing themselves for this situation. NESA's profiling must also be seen as a preparation for the liberalisation of the electricity market in Denmark. NESA profiles itself in several ways. In this paper, is described how NESA tries to make its customers take interest in their electricity and energy consumption and simultaneously make them aware of who their electricity supplier is. This effort is aimed at all customers even though the measures for the various customer groups differ.

articleTitle: Integration of energy and information: multima
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Dutch consumers use various types of commodities, such as electricity, gas, water and heating. In practice, all these commodities are located in one central space, together with the incoming TV-cable and telephone lines. In 1994, Nolec, Schlumberger, Landmark (design office) and NUON (a large Dutch electric utility) started a pilot project to establish whether a meter cupboard could be developed with smaller dimensions and greater functionality. It also had to be suitable for energy management by consumers. The objective was to locate the incoming electricity, gas and water supplies and communication functions in one meter cupboard, thus saving considerable space. All relevant information concerning the consumption of these commodities had to be able to be read on the spot from the associated meters or remotely from a central display or PC. It also had to be possible for both the supply board and the consumers to control the consumption. The pilot project was a complete success. Holec and Schlumberger therefore decided to establish a co-operation to produce and market this integrated unit under the name MULTIMA.

articleTitle: Interaction of active compensators and rectifier loads
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: When trying to reduce the distortion of the mains voltage-caused by rectifier loads with capacitive smoothing (RCS)-either with active or passive filters or with harmonic compensators, two particular effects amongst others are to be observed: the reaction of the rectifier current to the improved shape of the voltage; and the multiple change of the power system impedance during one period. This paper deals with both of these effects.

articleTitle: Results of a comprehensive comparative test program on 36 kV cable accessories
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: From November 1995 to June 1996, LABORELEC carried out a comprehensive test program on cable accessories for 36 kV networks. This report treats comparative tests on 36 kV indoor terminations, straight joints and plug-in cable systems for XLPE cable and transition joints between XLPE and paper cable. Tests were based on Belgian standards NBN C68-204, but were designed to obtain a maximum of information concerning the quality of today's technology in this field.

articleTitle: PREINV: a comprehensive tool for network installations planning
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology of a supportive application developed by Iberdrola and Software AG Espana to evaluate, compare and select different power system investment alternatives. The application integrates electric concepts like load flow solutions for radial networks, power losses and reliability analysis with economic variables like development costs, interest rates, life expectancy, etc., to allow Iberdrola's power network planning personnel to select the best investment alternative.

articleTitle: Home automation integration as a DSM incentive
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Information technology (IT) has taken a definite step into households. Already, many appliances and devices contain powerful intelligence such as home computers and video recorders. The next step is to integrate these devices. But still, most devices are unable to communicate and they are not connected to an appropriate information infrastructure. These facts imply that most opportunities to integrate and, thereby to accomplish synergy effects, are lost. This is indeed the situation for utilities aiming at demand side management (DSM), since they need direct or indirect access to appliances inside the household. This paper mainly addresses a mass market approach and stresses the importance of a cooperative approach for utilities and other actors. The purpose is to elucidate that an overall and long-term perspective is needed if the actors on the home-IT market should have a real chance to influence the IT-development in the homes from the start. The paper is based upon several industrial case studies carried out at the department of Industrial Control Systems at Royal Institute of Technology (KTH) in Stockholm, covering Swedish actors active within the field of bringing IT into the homes.

articleTitle: Safety of distribution transformers against internal failure
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Tests have been carried out by LABORELEC and PAUWELS, on ELECTRABEL's initiative, in order to verify the efficiency of current limiting fuses and overpressure detecting devices to avoid any external effect in case of transformer internal failure. The test programme was set up with the following objectives: to know the pressure/volume relationship for a transformer tank of the type used on the network; to know the highest pressure in service, including overloading conditions; to know the pressure withstand limit; to know the time and current limits for the tank withstand against internal failure; to investigate the behaviour of arcs in oil; to make full scale tests with simulation of different types of faults; and to check the working of two types of pressure detecting devices. The tests have been done on hermetically sealed transformers which therefore have a specific design of the tank and cooling ribs. For the considered transformers, the tests have confirmed the efficiency of the fuse protection which could prevent any external effect during the tests. Despite those results and of the good service performance, one can not completely exclude that a fault in the secondary windings causes a pressure rise which goes beyond the tank withstand limit, but those can be controlled by a complementary protection using pressure detection.

articleTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)

articleTitle: Reliability of medium voltage primary substation structures
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: One of the top priorities of EDF's (France) corporate strategic plan is to improve the quality of electricity supplies. A main area of planned progress is the reduction in the frequency of major outages in densely populated urban areas which arise from the total or partial loss of primary substations. This paper describes how, since 1991, work has been undertaken with a view to improving the reliability of primary substations in urban areas.

articleTitle: Frequency of occurrence of lightning overvoltages on distribution lines
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The evaluation of lightning overvoltages on distribution lines has been a subject of intense studies and research in recent years, covering evaluation methodology, field observation of induced voltages and direct strokes, theory of voltage induction on lines, experiments with scale models, effectiveness of protection means such as installation of shield cable or arresters along the line and others. This paper presents a review of the evaluation methodology and discussion of some aspects related to the subject, including comparisons of the quantification of frequency of overvoltages with calculations performed with the striking distance according to the electrogeometrical model and Eriksson's model, and verification of the influence of considering the wave front time of lightning currents on induced voltages estimated by Rusck's theory.

articleTitle: An evaluation of the environmental impact and of the safety of compact and modular equipment using SF6 up to 36 kV
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: In high voltage electrical installations (up to 36 kV), there has recently been a considerable increase in the use of compact and modular equipment whose insulation and cut-off medium is SF/sub 6/ gas. The reasons for this increase are: enhanced reliability; improved degree of safety; zero maintenance; and a huge reduction in volume. Pure SF/sub 6/ is an innocuous gas. It is assigned a threshold limit value (TLV) similar to that for any inoffensive gas not present in the usual working atmosphere, and its use can present new environmental conditions in transformer substations. This paper examines the most extreme environmental situations that can occur inside a transformer substation caused by accidental gas leaks, such as oxygen displacement, and the concentration of by-products for each situation, and their comparison with the TLVs required by the ACGIH (American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists). Cases examined are: during the installation of equipment; during the equipment working life; due to internal arcing; and during the recovery of the equipment.

articleTitle: Measured and perceived quality: conclusions of the experiment named QUALIMAT
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: EDF conducted a measurement program over three years, from June 1993 to June 1996. Its purpose was to measure power quality, customers' opinion and the connection between them. Three hundred measuring devices (Qualimetre) were installed at the premises of industrial customers between June 1993 and June 1995. The QUALIMAT experiment gathered such a huge quantity of data that it enabled us to study the influence of system characteristics on the power quality and the effect of power disturbances on customers' opinions. This paper presents the results of the equipment: correlations between measured power quality and customers' opinion, statistics on the measurements of voltage dips, short interruptions, harmonic currents and unbalance, correlations between system characteristics and disturbances, model of the number of interruptions and voltage dips as a function of system characteristics.

articleTitle: Distributed intelligence in tomorrow's distribution system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: This paper describes how deregulation of the European energy market will force electric utilities to focus on efficiency and power quality. The MV and LV distribution network will be an important target for utilities to reduce life cycle cost and increase customer value. The authors describe how ABB have prepared for this new market environment by investing in long-term R&D programs as well as development projects with distributed intelligent control products being introduced on the market in 1997/1998.

articleTitle: Analysis on reliability of urban power supply of Shandong network of China in 1995
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Power supply reliability (rate) directly reflects the capability of a network in supplying power to its customers. Through reliability analysis, it is possible to locate major factors in links of power generation, transmission and distribution that affect the reliability of power supply and to put forward measures for improvement. This paper makes an analysis of the reliability of the urban power supply of the Shandong power network, China, in 1995.

articleTitle: Electrical ageing test of connectors used on overhead (OH) aerial bundled conductors (ABC)
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Equipment of the junction connector or derivation connector type used on the French low voltage overhead (OH) aerial bundled conductors (ABC) were subjected to the following test procedure: insulated conductor connection equipment for low voltage aerial networks and services. Electrical ageing test: HN 33-E-61 (August 1985). This work, conducted within a mixed workgroup composed of manufacturers, users (EDF) and independent laboratories, has brought some precision on various points, which can lead to better reproducibility of tests. These tests permitted validation the existing product standards, to complement and validate the C 33-004 test standard: Connection equipment for low voltage aerial networks and services with at least one insulated conductor-Electrical ageing test.

articleTitle: Improvement of quality service in Uruguay-plans developed and its results in the period 93-95. Fault statistic as a parameter of measurement
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The present paper aims to describe the improvement process of the quality of the product and the technical service that has been undertaken by the UTE electric utility (Uruguay) since 1990 and to show the obtained results so far as well as the actions foreseen in the future. It develops the institutional framework and the countrywide context in which the activity of UTE is developed. The current situation and the improvement for Montevideo, capital city of Uruguay, are described. Finally, the paper contains a brief description of the plans and actions that UTE is developing in facing the changes to the environment that the approval of the regulative frame for electric utilities could produce.

articleTitle: Optimum design and dimensioning of power supply systems in the automobile industry
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Reliable and economical solutions are required for supply and distribution of electrical energy for the processes employed in industrial plants. On the basis of the power supply concept for the automobile industry, the authors show that such solutions can be achieved only by interlinking power system planning and system engineering.

articleTitle: Statistical study of lightning induced overvoltages on distribution power lines and risk analysis
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Owing to the increasing sensitivity of low voltage electrical equipment, it is necessary to be able to assess the magnitude of overvoltages caused by lightning. These are the most problematic overvoltages and, for the most part, they travel through power distribution lines. A risk analysis must be conducted to assist the decision to install a protective device on a given installation. In the French approach, the first stage of this analysis is the evaluation of the level of exposure to lightning induced overvoltages. The second stage consists in allowing for a criterion to evaluate the consequences of these electrical disturbances (destruction or unavailability of equipment) for a given level of exposure and in a given situation. This decision aid method is empirical. It is based on the main characteristics of the electric power supply and on the level of lightning strike density in the relevant area. An analysis of the same type is proposed on a complementary basis by two IEC committees. Finally, a calculation tool (Anastasia) was developed in order to allow the accurate quantification of the level of overvoltages on an installation. It is based on modelling of the coupling of the lightning channel and a power distribution line, allowing overvoltages to be calculated with the EMTP program. The Monte Carlo method is then used, in combination with simulations, to obtain a statistical distribution of the stresses at a given point. A comparison was made between the results obtained with Anastasia and the measurements conducted on an installation in the context of a campaign organized for several years by France Telecom.

articleTitle: Quality of service in the Netherlands
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Growing competition between utilities, changing legislation and increased usage of sensitive and disturbing end-user equipment, are some reasons for growing attention for the customers' view towards the product electricity and its related services. This growing interest certainly does not mean that the technical quality level always has to be increased. This depends mainly on the requirements and expectations of the customers. Achieving a reliable power supply at high quality level requires enormous investments. For electric utilities, it is important to know how the customers value the delivered products and services. Utilities need new tools and techniques to search for an optimal quality level for each customer. Product differentiation and additional services can be developed if the right information is available. In 1994 KEMA started a project called: quality of service. During the project different methods and techniques have been developed. In this paper three tools are presented. The "customer simulator", the Dutch power quality monitoring programme and the "PSQ-indicator".

articleTitle: Problems encountered with connecting decentralized generating plants to the distribution networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Since the early 1990s there has been a surge in the number of decentralized generating facilities connected to the distribution network. The problems encountered are not new in themselves-what is new is the large number of applications the distributor now finds itself confronted with. Small installations are usually barely economically viable so given the modest size of decentralized generation the cost of the disconnection protection should not be prohibitive. While this is a demanding technique the engine-network interface must be sufficiently simple to make the project worthwhile. What is more, the large number of installations means that it is impossible to opt for any solution which would require constant surveillance. This technique concerns decentralized generation of up to 15 MVA operating in parallel on the distribution networks. We examine the steps that need to be taken to ensure a suitable connection with the distributor's low and medium voltage networks which are assumed to be fully earthed. The target is the network protection and operating personnel safety. A distinction is drawn between in-plant generation and independent generation because a different system may need to be set up depending on circumstances. The aim of independent generation is to supply the network, while the primary aim of in-plant generation is to supply the generator's own equipment and can supply the excess power to the network if required.

articleTitle: Concept for optimised operation of distribution networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The EU Energy Market has been opened to limited competition, as the EU Energy Ministers adopted the proposed Directive on these issues. This Directive shall transpose into national Deregulation Laws in each EU member state, at the latest by 1 January 1999. The important provision of the Directive, relevant for this paper, is the goal of Creating More Competitive Production and Distribution Utilities. The message of this paper is that electric utilities will have to continuously analyse their situation on their network operational performance, find and optimise their operational cost object function. This function will comprise mainly cost for reactive and active compensation, quality (availability, reliability, voltage quality, etc.), component operation and maintenance. These analyses will reveal the weak areas of each utility's network operation and help finding where the efforts for improvement shall take place. This also implies that the network design and upgrading philosophy constantly have to be developed, in order to decide whether traditional reinforcements and/or expansions are cost beneficial, or when new technology solutions compete and beat the traditional investment schemes.

articleTitle: Failures clarification of MV nonmetallic screened aerial bundled cables
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Medium voltage nonmetallic screened aerial bundled cable (ABC) has been used in Brazil for 20 years as a solution for substation exits, narrow streets and crossings. The benefits of such cables are well known. This simple cable construction has been appointed by some customers as the reason for an unexpected number of in-service failures. During the survey of plausible causes of failures several hypotheses have emerged, including an unsuitable electric field control, since the polymeric semiconducting outer layer (SMC) does not have the same characteristics of a metallic screen. This work reports the cable behaviour when subjected to a multi-stress test that simulates operation conditions, aiming to clarify failure mechanisms of such cables.

articleTitle: Damage detection and repair measures regarding medium-voltage latticed towers
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: When medium-voltage overhead power lines have been in service for many years, the network operators usually find themselves confronted with the question of how to maintain their system on a methodical, efficient and cost-effective basis. This requires a systematic analysis of the actual condition of the system, which implies assessing the quality of a rather extensive network of lines that has been expanded in the course of time but has not always been sufficiently documented. If we take a look at the history of the medium-voltage overhead line network as it presents itself in Germany, it is obvious that the network operators will be faced with the fact that maintenance and reconstruction measures of a fundamental kind will become necessary in the future, since the majority of lines will reach an age of between 40-60 years within the next decade. This is particularly true for latticed steel towers because this type of mast have now been in service for a very long time. In this paper, the authors show how network operators might proceed in order to assess the current quality and condition of such steel towers and to develop adequate and efficient reconstruction concepts.

articleTitle: Supply continuity in an industrial plant with internal generation: field measurements for the dynamic performance assessment
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Field measurements of long-term dynamic phenomena inside an industrial power plant connected to the public distribution network were carried out in order to assess the performance of the power system with its internal generating units. To this end, perturbations were intentionally produced by suitable manipulation of the control variables such as boiler master control (fuel), feedwater and speed governor. The long-term dynamic is of strong interest since, even if the supply in the industrial plant survives short term transients (transient stability), then it could be unable to maintain its frequency due to the inadequacy of the boiler power response. The recorded variables were: electric active power delivered by the two generating units; frequency; steam and feedwater pressure; steam temperature; steam, feedwater and fuel flow; and boiler level. Such measurement results could later be used to validate a model of a typical industrial power plant boiler suitable for the simulation of all kinds of long-term phenomena.

articleTitle: How to conciliate demand side management and electromagnetic compatibility?
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Since 1993, the French National Electricity Utility, Electricite de France (EDF), and the French Environment and Energy Agency (ADEME) have worked together for the promotion of energy saving on electricity use, for better satisfaction of customers and a global national interest. These demand side management programs, especially on their customers service approach have been already discussed in several papers, and are focused as follow: lighting; domestic appliances; buildings; industry, especially with variable speed drive for electric motor; and, isolated areas. Drives and particular lights absorb currents with high harmonics content, which in some cases can cause problems on the customers plant itself, and which can also pollute neighbouring plants. Furthermore, EDF has engagement on the quality of the voltage delivered to its customers, and therefore needs to control the harmonics level in its distribution networks. Efforts have been developed to conciliate this problem of electromagnetic network compatibility and with the wish of EDF to go through DSM programs. These aspects are developed in the paper.

articleTitle: Contributions to applying the RCM (reliability centered maintenance) in power installations
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Reliability centred maintenance (RCM) represents a conception of using the feedback of power installations field operation in the predictive maintenance of such equipment based on their reliability calculations. The present paper proves, using new arguments, the influence of technological designs upon certain power apparatus maintenance strategies. From the analyses and considerations made, an obvious opportunity of more extended research in the field exists.

articleTitle: Digital technology for switchboards the key to a new age in switchboard design
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: This paper describes how the use of modern information techniques the standard fitting of a freely programmable switchbay control unit and the use of modern sensors have led to the extensively standardised switchboard ZX1 with secondary systems being type tested for the first time. The new switchboard technology with a stainless steel enclosed, gas-insulated core module, together with the use of vacuum circuit breakers, guarantees extensive freedom from maintenance. A high degree of standardisation without impairment of flexibility for the user significantly shortens planning, assembly and commissioning time.

articleTitle: Experimentation of a SCADA/DMS-GIS interface development
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The paper deals with the development of an interface between a SCADA/DMS system (supervisory control and data acquisition/distribution management system) and a GIS (geographical information system), at a French utility. First, it explains how the technical need of this utility evolved and why this interface became necessary: installation of a GIS to manage the whole electrical network equipments; and SCADA system evolution into a more complete DMS, due to the more and more automated network exploitation. Secondly, the development of this interface based on the EDIGe/spl acute/O norm is presented in detail. Then, the conclusion shows the need of the normalization of the conceptual models describing the electrical network, in order to utilize the open architecture of DMS systems.

articleTitle: The new procedure to support investments plans in ENEL MV distribution
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The report describes the new control techniques used by ENEL in defining investments for MV distribution networks to meet the load growth, to improve the supply quality and the network performance and to solve critical situations due to plants obsolescence or to environmental problems. To fulfil the above mentioned goals new software, was introduced that makes use of a suitable set of indices, provided by the information system describing the MV distribution network. The indices concern quality of supply, network performance, plants obsolescence and environmental problems. The procedure guides the operator in defining the priorities of investigation among different critical circuits, in choosing the optimum reinforcement alternative for each critical situation and in defining priorities of investments among different critical situations. The report gives a description of the main indices considered in terms of actual, constraint, threshold and target values. A general overview of the different phases of the procedure is then presented: selection of the critical network situations choice of the most suitable remedies, evaluation of costs and indices improvements for each intervention considered, upstream aggregation of costs and indices improvements.

articleTitle: Reliability indices estimation of unstationary distribution networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The paper presents an efficient and overall analytical approach towards the prognosis of reliability indices in the process of development of medium voltage city distribution networks. The presented model gives possibility for estimation of duration of the interruption of supply of the load points in question, due to unexpected failure at some, arbitrarily chosen, element of radial distributive network. Repair crew movement during searching for the faulted cable section is modeled, in order to estimate time needed for isolation and renewal of supply of load points. The differences in strategies of searching and isolating of the faulted section are also taken into consideration. The reliability analysis is possible in the case that the dispatcher and the crew for maintenance search for the section by use of halving method or by the method of measuring the resistance of isolation using megaommeter. Application of the model and developed computer program is illustrated on the example of the real network of the city of Novi Sad. Some feeders are analyzed as unstationary elements which during the planned period change the configuration, number of load points, load and unit outage costs. The change of configuration is manifested by connection of new MV/LV substations between the existing ones, or by prolongation of lines. The change of the configuration of open loop depending on link arrangement is considered. The results give a real reliability picture of the present but also of the future MV network. In addition, data thus obtained can be used as basic ones for the estimation of benefits in cost-benefit analyses.

articleTitle: Intelligent MV circuit-breakers: recent evolutions
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: With the recent evolution of circuit breaking chambers, high current interruption is no longer a problem. The more profitable benefits, both on the technological and the economical points of view, lead to an increase of the added value of a circuit-breaker in the power network. Soon it will also be possible to integrate the circuit-breaker in the managing process of a substation, by using a digital linkage to the drive. By introducing a new drive principle, based on an asymmetrical magnetic actuator, the operating mechanism can be very simple and will integrate directly this communication philosophy. It is assumed that the standards will rapidly define the communication protocols between devices. This is already the subject of an IEC working group.

articleTitle: Determination of zero impedance of 3-phase-current transformers by measurements
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Special difficulties arise in ascertaining zero impedances of 3-phase-current oil power transformers. Basic conditions for a zero-current flow and thus the acting of a zero impedance in a power transformer are at least a star- (Y-) connected winding and an earthed neutral. Systems with low-resistance and short-time earthing require exact knowledge of the transformers' zero impedance for the calculation of the fault current. Due to the complex electrical and magnetic interactions in the transformer, especially in polyphase transformers with several counter-current conducting windings, ascertaining of the zero impedances is practically only possible by measurement. Proceeding from a classification of transformers according to their design properties, a possibility to assume zero impedances of power transformers of similar designs is created. The mathematical modelling of the transformer, transformer classification, and measurement and calculation of the zero impedance are discussed.

articleTitle: Digital distance relay brings advantages of full-scheme relays to distribution networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Faster and faster development in the sector of electronic components and the increased use of automation in power network management and electric installations, have led to sophisticated equipment, incorporating functions which, until recently and even now, have been carried out by separate units. Improved performance has lessened and, in some cases, completely removed the differences between devices used for transmission and for distribution. The power system protection relay described in this paper is therefore aimed at the widest possible market, without prejudice to performance and user costs.

articleTitle: ENEL's DSM actions in the international scenario
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: In the framework of national policies, which, since the end of the 1970s have had the target of making consumers rationally use natural sources, in particular energy, and in the pursuit of environmental goals, the Governments and the utilities have driven several DSM actions in many countries. The activities implemented by ENEL have included the analysis of the different components of the energy drain, from the primary sources to the final use in industry, agriculture, residential and commercial buildings. This is in order to improve the energy efficiency by new electrotechnologies and more effective appliances. Moreover ENEL has carried out commercial initiatives by specific contractual agreements based on the marginal costs of the electric service. The paper explains ENEL's strategies and the actions implemented by the utility on DSM; the results in terms of energy efficiency, electric demand dynamics and of load curve changing are also explained. Finally the paper explores the DSM perspectives in the Italian future scenario, where energy companies will act in a more competitive market.

articleTitle: A national approach to power quality and the minimization of negative impacts on an economy
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: South Africa's National Electricity Regulator (NER) has the primary aims of reducing the cost of electricity, ensuring equity and sustaining electrification. The regulator has further declared the intent to regulate issue and retention of licenses to generate, transmit and distribute electricity on the basis of minimum technical quality of supply (QOS) as well as quality of service standards. The electricity supply industry has at the regulator's request developed a set of minimum technical standards for quality of supply and a set of service quality standards. Eskom the large parastatal electricity utility has over three years developed a product orientated approach to the quality of electricity. This paper describes the role of technical QOS standards and the economic application of the network and highly leveraged "behind the meter" approaches to quality of supply problems.

articleTitle: Prefactibility study for the widespread installation of the SLACE system ~electricity telemetering\
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The main objective of the SLACE system (automatic reading of electricity meters) is to obtain automatic readings from customer's watthour meters, but it also offers other additional uses. The system comprises a series of different units which are all interconnected in different ways. Its characteristics and functions are described in this paper.

articleTitle: Power resupply means and live works: two complementary ways of reducing power cuts for works
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Power system resupply means make use of live-line working techniques since optimum use requires live connection to the network, in MV or in LV. Therefore, such techniques result in a quantitative increase in the number of operations carried out live at low voltage. Connecting resupply means on-load requires live electrical operations, such as putting voltages in phase, two LV networks in parallel and synchronization between power networks with different frequencies, all which must be done by qualified and specially trained personnel. Therefore, qualitatively, improved conventional live-line working techniques are required. As such, the authors argue that resupply means should be considered as complementary to, rather than competing with, live-line working. In such a scheme, the operator knows that there is a complete range of means available to him to prevent power cuts and he is free to choose the most suitable means while optimizing costs.

articleTitle: The effects of wind, snow and ice on optical fibre systems on overhead line conductors
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The problems created by the effects of wind, snow and ice loadings on overhead line conductors have been studied for many years. Dampers are used to control aeolian vibration and galloping and various devices are in use to attempt to restrict heavy snow/ice loads. However, in addition to these dedicated devices, many networks are being used to transmit data using a variety of optical fibre systems. These include fibres contained within metal conductors and fibres wrapped externally onto the conductors. Fibre optic systems are also used in a self-supporting mode known as ADSS. EA Technology has been involved over the last eight years in the remote monitoring of test spans and samples of overhead line conductors in the UK in areas chosen for their severe weather. The sites are unmanned and regularly suffer gales, blizzards and severe icing conditions. These sites were therefore ideally suited to the investigation into the effects of these conductor mounted devices on the performance of the line. This paper details the optical fibre systems, the test sites and their monitoring techniques and the results obtained.

articleTitle: Strategic system planning of an urban power system for 60000 inhabitants
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Planning experience is documented with the practical example of the town of Singen (Germany), located to the west of Lake Constance, supplied by the Gasand Elektrizitaetswerk Singen (GEWS). Since the turn of the century, the town of Singen has had a public power supply system for what was then 2500 inhabitants. After an eventful history of remarkable urban development and industrialization, 1996 sees the power supply system celebrating the centenary of its existence. Pending system improvement measures, such as cable and switchgear requirements, the differing system operating voltages of 20 and 16 kV, different suppliers with differing HV levels of 110 and 50 kV, decisions concerning new electricity supply agreements to be concluded and preparation for increased system automation were the reasons for commissioning this system upgrade study.

articleTitle: Voltage control in medium-voltage distribution networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Voltage control becomes increasingly important in medium-voltage distribution networks. A new tool to optimise voltage control in the medium-voltage distribution network and thus enable utilities to obtain, maintain and guarantee systematically an optimal quality of supply has been developed. This paper describes both the methodology to optimise voltage control and the experiences at MEGA Limburg, a regional utility in the Netherlands, which applies this tool in network planning practice.

articleTitle: Retrofit in asset life management
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The electricity supply industry in the United Kingdom is based on a distribution system which was established predominantly in the 1950s and 1960s. The Regional Electricity Companies (RECs) therefore have a large population of equipment such as high-voltage switchgear which is nearing the age where its replacement will be required. Manufacturers have begun to recognise the challenges and opportunities that this brings, and some are now offering products and services that provide realistic options for asset life management. This paper focuses on the need for replacement of high-voltage switchgear (11 kV) and discusses the option of retrofitting new vacuum circuit breakers into existing switchboards. The paper is based on the experiences of one UK Regional Electricity Company-London Electricity (LE)-and a manufacturer of high voltage switchgear-Reyrolle Projects Ltd. Retrofit has been successfully applied at a number of the RECs substations. The constraints in carrying out replacement at live operational substations was an important consideration in selecting the option of retrofit and the learning points of this experience are discussed. Provision of control facilities new circuit was an added benefit as was the replacement of electro-mechanical relays with digital (microprocessor) relays, providing enhanced information and communications.

articleTitle: Iberdrola's alarms management system ~power network protection\
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Iberdrola (Spain) has developed a corporate alarms management system (codename ALARMS) that acquires, in near real-time, the alarms, the events and messages produced by the 25 transmission and distribution control systems, stores them in several relational database servers and allows corporative access to them. ALARMS has a range of users, ranging from network operators to protections, maintenance, planning, control and communications engineers. Access is performed using a client/server system, with a number of facilities for searching, storage and printing. The development has been very cost-effective as it is based on standard products: the different operative systems used DOS, Unix and Windows are employed where appropriate, the communication protocol-all communications are TCP/IP based, the programming languages-C, PRO*C and Visual Basic, and finally a relational database server.

articleTitle: Technical conditions for the connection of generating facilities to the medium voltage network development of a 175 Hz active filter for independent power producers
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: This paper describes an initial investigation which focused on the technical conditions of connecting power facilities from 1 MW to 10 MW onto MV power systems. Wind power plants, and the technical connection conditions for installations larger than 10 MW on MV power systems, are now being examined. The results of these investigations show that the development of decentralised power generating schemes connected to networks initially designed to distribute electricity poses numerous problems. As long as this generation remains marginal in relation to consumption, it can be evaluated under acceptable conditions, thanks to the capacity of the receiving power system; as soon as it grows beyond the marginal level, the problems to be solved bring the actual design of these power systems into question. This is a particularly sensitive issue for rural distribution networks where problems concerning protection schemes and, above all, voltage stability are worrying.

articleTitle: Chemical moisture barrier power and control cable for petrochemical plants and refineries
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: A new cable sheath technology has been developed to address the chemical, and contamination in cables rated through 138 kV. The sheath design is based on the use of copolymer coated metal tapes bonded to a plastic oversheath. The "bonded" or "laminate" construction is commonly called a "chemical moisture barrier" (CMB) sheath. The tapes frequently serve a dual function by providing electrical shielding as well as chemical and moisture protection. The components of the CMB sheath, starting from the outside of the cable, are the plastic oversheath, copolymer coated metallic tape as shield and chemical-moisture barrier, sealed overlap, inner jacket (optional), and the cable core. The performance benefits associated with the specification, selection, installation, and operation of CMB sheathed cable for use in industrial and utility electrical systems are described.

articleTitle: Simplification of medium voltage networks versus a higher degree of guarantee
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The Universal Fair of Seville, popularly know as EXPO'92, took place from April to October 1992. The land situated on the "Isla de la Cartuja" was built on and inhabited for this event, and two HV/MV substations were built to supply the MV/LV centres via a 20 kV underground network. These centres supplied electricity to the pavilions that were erected, and the installations of associated services. Once the Fair was over and some of the participating countries' pavilions taken down, several of the MV/LV substations were dismounted leaving the network in that area with the same configuration as today. In this study we establish comparisons between this newer, simply designed and remote controlled network, and the network in the city of Seville which has elements of different ages and the typical complexity of networks that have been built in stages.

articleTitle: Measurement processing for generalized use CPGV
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The establishment of the characteristics of voltage supplied by the distribution networks is the result of the asymptotic evolution of the concepts of emission, immunity and electromagnetic compatibility for satisfying the expectations of the users and the electrical energy suppliers. The common point of reference is to be found in the standard EN 50160 which indicates the values expected of the characteristics at any point in the electrical network under normal operating conditions without establishing any geographical restrictions. Experiences in the use of a standard format for measuring voltage dips and short interruptions, the measurement of variations in voltage and the definition of a format for measuring harmonics, pulses and flicker are given in the report. The main advantage of this work system is the independence between the software design for evaluation and the use of one or various equipment for recording the characteristics according to EN 50160. Lastly, the use of homogeneous criteria results rebounds in clarity between the user and the distributor which makes a comparison and accumulation of results, obtained in various companies, periods of time and countries, possible and also provides a tool for verifying the improvements produced in different periods through investments made in the network.

articleTitle: Development of RENEL Sibiu's SCADA and monitoring system and improvement of protective system handling digital protection integrated into SCADA systems
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The paper presents the adopted concept in implementing the supervision, control, monitoring and protection functions for 110 kV and 20 kV substations. The article describes the structure of the existing SCADA system, the approach adopted in implementing new facilities, the main performances of RTUs and the main functions of the computer-based control and monitoring centre. The concept of open systems architecture adopted for the SCADA system inherently offers an increased control system availability and improved upgradeability. The authors also present the development and the main algorithms used to achieve a digital protection equipment for medium voltage (MV) power systems. The equipment includes protection functions, automation functions as well as metering functions for isolated neutral networks or earthing through a resistor or an arc suppression coil. An important task of the equipment is the capability to be integrated in SCADA systems.

articleTitle: A bi-directional communication system based on power line carriers
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: In this paper, the authors describe an automated system which uses the distribution network as a communication media for connecting an electricity supply utility with its customers. This system was the outcome of an international research project jointly undertaken by Landis and Gyr and the Greek electricity supply company PPC (Public Power Corporation). The design and implementation phase took place in Switzerland, whereas the installation, testing and evaluation phases were carried out in Athens. The purpose of the project was to investigate the technical feasibility of two-way communications through the distribution lines of the PPC network and to demonstrate the potential benefits of such an approach for both the utility and the consumers.

articleTitle: A novel electromagnetic compensator
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Nowadays, power quality concerns are bringing important challenges to industrial and utility engineers. In general, due to the proliferation of nonlinear loads, electric signals are unbalanced, asymmetric and distorted. As an alternative to solve these problems, this paper presents a proposal for a novel electromagnetic compensator. This equipment can be helpful: (1) in the load flow control; (2) to feed static multiconverter systems, replacing with some advantages the commonly used delta/zig-zag transformers, to reduce or even to eliminate the characteristic harmonics; and (3) to correct voltage drops and unbalances simultaneously, as an alternative to the conventional solution obtained by line drop compensators.

articleTitle: New flexible 12-24 kV cable system for rural distribution
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: This report presents a new developed flexible distribution system over long distances for 12-24 kV and power ratings of 3000 kVA (max 10 MVA). The XLPE-insulated three core cables have been specially design for aerial application on poles as well as for traditional underground and under water use. The new cable system is economically very competitive when compared to traditional systems and presents many overriding technical advantages. More than 500 in air installations have been successfully undertaken during a two year period.

articleTitle: SYNOPTRA-synthesis of optimal overhead lines
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: A method aiming at the generation of optimal overhead lines is presented; it is implemented in a computer program named SYNOPTRA. The optimisation refers to the right-of-way as well as to the number of pylons and their heights. Each overhead line generated considers the topology of the given area and strictly follows all the technical specifications such as the minimal distances between conductor and earth. Due to the complexity of the task, there exists no analytical method for solving this problem. This paper describes the application of a probabilistic method, an adapted version of the evolutionary algorithms, to the above mentioned problem and presents an approach to consider multiple objectives in this case "visibility", approval ability and "costs" ("multiobjective optimisation").

articleTitle: The application of fundamental network modelling tools
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The goal of any distribution network manager is to operate the network as close as possible to its limits, whilst observing the constraints of fault levels, voltage tolerance, stability and reliability. However, the ever improving quality of data available to managers presents real problems when using previous network analysis techniques, limited either by the mathematical models employed or the effort needed to convert from a simple balanced to a full unbalanced model of the network. This paper describes experiences with one development, the Unbalanced Loadflow (UBLF) module employed in the DINIS suite from ICL, and examines a number of networks requiring such analysis, comparing the results against conventional positive sequence studies where possible.

articleTitle: Overvoltages Due To Vacuum Switches And Their Reduction In M.V. Networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)

articleTitle: Dutch distribution cable: improvements in construction, reliability, environment and efficiency
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: In this paper the existing medium voltage cable grid in the Netherlands is shown. The perfect performance of these cables is responsible for the very short outage times in our country. Typical is the belted paper 12 kV cable with a very good performance since 1905. However, problems with this type of cable have occurred more frequently. With the arrival of the newly developed 12 kV three phase XLPE cable we can solve the paper cable problems. The main solution is using the XLPE cable for high and strongly changing loads. For the normal thin distribution cables the existing paper cable can be used for more than 40 years. The future development of cable systems will be in two ways: firstly by diagnostics like 0.1 Hz partial discharge measurements; and secondly by monitoring and by protection with integrated fibre optics in all types of power cables. With these developments we will come to 'total cable management'.

articleTitle: Integrated resources planning at CEB-Brasilia city utility
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Due to the fact that CEB electric utility (Brazil) depends almost totally on external generation, buying 95% of the energy that it distributes, the development of studies that compare the supply options with load management alternatives is of large interest. This dependency makes the utility vulnerable to the institutional changes in the Brazilian electric sector and even concerning the oscillation of possible supply tariff (buying) and distribution (selling). This paper contains the description of the methodology used for the comparative studies among the supply options and the demand side management programs.

articleTitle: Reliability and cost evaluation of switchgear configurations in HV/MV substations
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Reliability and cost evaluation of switchgear configurations in HV/MV substations are described. The evaluation methodology is used to analyse projects at four Norwegian electric utilities. One of these projects is presented. The results show that the total equipment and interruption costs will be lowest by using simple switchgear solutions. This paper describes how the switchgear configurations in HV/MV substations can be simplified without reducing the reliability to an unacceptable level. The reliability calculations show that simplification in some cases even will increase the reliability.

articleTitle: Energy conservation strategies applied to demand management
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: The paper describes the principal characteristics of the "energy conservation strategies simulator-SECON Model" an important tool for planning actions of the "National Program Of Energy Conservation-PROCEL", in final uses field. First, the document presents some fundamental definitions about conservation. After this, the paper describes the structure of SECON's models: residential, industrial, commercial, economic analysis and ranking. The main part of the methodology consists in simulating the different strategies of some variables evolution (market, efficiency rates, acceptance, etc.) for later verifying of the conservation goals in "MWh conserved" in the medium/long terms. Once presented the set of programs to be developed, the system gives the priorities for the alternatives proposed as a function of the established criterias in accordance with the specialist's opinions. At the end, the paper shows some conclusions about the system use at PROCEL works, and gives some practical results with methodology application. In this way, SECON is an important instrument in demand management resulting from the final users of electric energy.

articleTitle: SMES systems applications to improve quality service
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: This article presents the contribution of SMES (superconducting magnetic energy storage) systems to the improvement quality of electricity supply service, either as a mitigating element or as a power support for critical loads. It also describes these systems and its operation. Finally, a description is shown of the state-of-the-art of this technology in Spain, as developed to date in the AMAS500 project.

articleTitle: Acceptance tests conducted on optical ground wires for checking additional fibre length
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference and Exhibition on Electricity Distribution. Part 1. Contributions (IEE Conf. Publ. No. 438)
abstract: Optical fibres integrated into overhead phase and earth conductors have been more and more used as communication links in the context of high voltage transmission line networks. In designing and manufacturing these conductors it is essential to take account of the fact that the glass fibre is highly sensitive to axial and lateral strain as well as bending. The quality of the system-meaning optical fibre and surrounding conductor structure-can only be assessed by carrying out tests which simulate real-life loads. This means taking into account not only those parts of the stranded conductor that are in direct contact with the glass fibre-such as the gel, for example-but the entire system, including also the connections and fixing means. The authors describe the acceptance and creep tests for these cables.

articleTitle: Long term investigation of thermal behaviour of 110 kV underground transmission lines in the Belgrade area
